newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: FOCUS-Saudi power firm signs deals worth $309 mln.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Saudi power firm signs deals worth $309 mln.

text.p: A major Saudi Arabian electricity company on Tuesday awarded four contracts worth 1.159 billion riyals ($309 million) to integrate its new power plant into the main power system to keep pace with surging domestic demand.
Chairman of the Saudi Consolidated Electric Company - East (SCECO-East) Feheid Fahad al-Shareef signed the contracts with the companies in the eastern city of Dammam.

The largest contract worth 558 million riyals was awarded to electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG for the construction of the Al-Fadhil high voltage substation and reinforcement of the 230 kilovolt system.

A second contract worth 405 million riyals went to India's KEC International and Saudi Arabia's Al-Sharif Group for Trading & Contracting for the construction of two 380 kilovolt transmission lines linking the new power plant, Ghazlan II, with the Al-Fadhil substation.
Saudi Services for Electro Mechanic Works Company Limited won a 106 million riyal contract to build 230 kilovolt transmission lines in the nearby industrial city of Jubail and surrounding areas.
SCECO-East awarded Marubeni Saudi Arabia Company Limited, a subsidiary of Marubeni Corp of Japan, a 88 million riyal contract for the expansion of a substation.
The four projects were due to be completed in 1999 and would integrate Ghazlan II into the main system of SCECO-East.

Last year, SCECO-East awarded Mitsubishi Heavy Industries a 4.155 billion riyal contract to build the 2,400-megawatt Ghazlan II plant, which consists of four units, each with a capacity of 600 megawatts.
The first unit is expected to come on stream in December 1999, the second in February 2000, the third in February 2001 and the fourth in February 2002.
Ghazlan II is part of an ambitious Saudi programme to raise the kingdom's power capacity to 60,000 megawatts over 25 years from the current 19,000 megawatts.

Shareef said when the projects are completed, they would help SCECO-East cater to the needs of the oil, basic and support industries in the kingdom and meet the burgeoning demand for power by residential and business sectors up to the year 2010.

He said SCECO-East would in two weeks sign a 10-year loan facility worth $500 million with local and international banks to finance part of the cost of the plant and associated projects. The rest will be financed through internal resources. ($1 = 3.75 riyals)
